lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about dreams.
My niece Aysu is six. Yesterday she said, "I want to be a doctor!"
That's a great job, a good job. I hope she is happy.
Today she said, "I want to be a singer." Then she said, "No. I want to be a dog."
A dog? Is that a job?
For Aysu, yes. She said, "A dog wakes up, eats, and sleeps. It is a good job!"
[laugh] That's a good dream. When I grow up, I want to be a dog too.
Sam, you are thirty-two. You are grown up, an adult.
Hmm. OK. Then my dream is a big race. One day I will run twenty-one kilometres.
Wow! How do you learn to run?
I study on the internet. And my friend Tom says, "Do not give up. Do not stop."
Good. Good luck, Sam!
Thank you! And what is your dream for the future, Leyla?
A very long sleep. Like a dog. [laugh] Bye for now!

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is dreams and goals.
Sam has a new goal. Tell everyone.
I'm going to run a half marathon. That's twenty-one kilometres, for the children's hospital. I have a plan. I practise three times a week.
How was the first practice?
Terrible. I ran for five minutes, then I lay on a bench. A grandmother with a shopping bag walked past me.
[laugh] So you failed?
I didn't fail. I just stopped. Then I found out there is a running club in my city. Twelve friendly people.
And you keep on running?
I keep on running. Every week I improve a little. Last Sunday I ran for forty minutes. I was so proud that I told my dad.
What did he say?
"Nice. Can you run and dance salsa at the same time?"
[laugh] Your dad is the best. What do you say when it's hard?
I say, "Never give up." And my friend Tom says, "Good luck with that!"
I think you will succeed. I'm looking forward to the race.
Me too. I can't wait. I just hope the grandmother with the bag is not there.
And my goal? My career is fine, but my dream job is...
A baker, like your dad. But you can't bake.
I know. I can only eat. That's also a career. See you next time!

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is ambition — what we really want from life.
Let's start with my cousin Rashad. He has a motorbike and a huge ambition: he wants to be a stunt rider.
That sounds dangerous.
Very. Last month he decided to go for it. His first challenge was to jump over a row of... cardboard boxes.
Cardboard boxes. OK. That's a small challenge.
Small, yes. But he failed. The boxes won. And his mother watched everything from the balcony.
[laugh] Go on. And what happened next?
He didn't give up. He's very determined. He asked a real stunt rider for help — a great opportunity — and now he trains with a coach. And he wears two helmets.
Smart. I think confidence comes from small steps. But you also need a role model. Who is yours?
My grandmother. She's eighty, she knits, she cheats at cards, and last year she learned video calls. She says, "The sky's the limit."
That's a good attitude. My dad used to say, "Aim high." And then he'd turn on the salsa.
Sam, are you ready to achieve your half marathon?
I think so. If I don't do it now, it's now or never. I'm going after it.
Failure scares everybody. But when you fail, you carry on. You try a different way.
Like Rashad and the boxes.
Exactly. A question for our listeners: what ambition would you go for this year, if nothing could stop you?
And please, nobody tell Rashad's mother. See you next time!
